nodes.summary: If `B` is a real Brownian motion, then almost surely, for every `a ∈ ℝ`, there is a time `t` with `B t = a`: the hitting time `T_a = inf {t ≥ 0 : B t = a}` is finite for every `a` (Le Gall, ENS notes *Intégration, Probabilités et Processus Aléatoires*, Corollaire 14.4.3, second assertion).
nodes.title: Linear Brownian motion hits every level

nodes.summary: For every exponent `α < 1/2` and every horizon `T`, almost every path of a Brownian motion is `α`-Hölder continuous on `[0, T]` (Le Gall, *Brownian Motion, Martingales, and Stochastic Calculus*, Chapter 2, section "The continuity of sample paths"). The proof applies Kolmogorov's lemma (Le Gall, DEA notes 1994, Lemme 2.3) to the moments `E |B t - B s|^β = c_β |t - s|^{β/2}`.
nodes.title: Hölder continuity of Brownian paths

nodes.summary: Brownian paths are nowhere differentiable (Paley, Wiener and Zygmund). Almost surely, the path `s ↦ B s ω` is differentiable at no time `t > 0` (Mörters and Peres, *Brownian Motion*, Cambridge University Press, 2010, Theorem 1.30). The statement is restricted to `t > 0` because the path is extended by `B 0` to negative times, so a two-sided derivative at `0` is not the Brownian one.
nodes.title: Brownian paths are nowhere differentiable

nodes.summary: If `B` is a real Brownian motion, then almost surely, for every level `A` and every `N`, there are integer times `n, m ≥ N` with `B n > A` and `B m < A`; in particular `limsup_{t → ∞} B t = +∞` and `liminf_{t → ∞} B t = -∞` (Le Gall, ENS notes *Intégration, Probabilités et Processus Aléatoires*, Corollaire 14.4.3, third assertion).
nodes.title: Brownian motion is unbounded above and below at infinity

nodes.summary: Every pre-Brownian motion `B` with measurable coordinates on a probability space has a modification `W` with measurable coordinates and continuous paths (on every sample), and `W` is a Brownian motion. The continuity comes from Kolmogorov's lemma (Le Gall, DEA notes 1994, Lemme 2.3), applied to the fourth moments of the increments. nodes.title: Brownian motion as a continuous modification of pre-Brownian motion

nodes.summary: There is a probability measure `μ` on the path space `ℝ≥0 → ℝ` and a process `W` on it with continuous paths (on every sample) that is a Brownian motion: its finite-dimensional laws are the Brownian ones (`W 0 = 0` a.s., independent centered Gaussian increments with variance the length of the time interval). nodes.title: Existence of Brownian motion

nodes.summary: For `β > 0`, `|x|^β` is integrable for the centered Gaussian law of any variance (all moments of a Gaussian are finite; Le Gall, *Brownian Motion, Martingales, and Stochastic Calculus*, Chapter 1).
nodes.title: Absolute moments of a centered Gaussian are integrable

nodes.summary: For `β ≥ 0`, `∫ |x|^β d N(0, v) = v^{β/2} ∫ |x|^β d N(0, 1)`, since `N(0, v)` is the image of `N(0, 1)` under `x ↦ √v x` (Le Gall, *Brownian Motion, Martingales, and Stochastic Calculus*, Chapter 1).
nodes.title: Scaling of the absolute moments of a centered Gaussian

nodes.summary: The fourth moment of the centered Gaussian law of variance `v` is `3 v²`, computed as the fourth derivative at `0` of its moment generating function `exp(v t² / 2)`; it is the moment used in Kolmogorov's criterion for Brownian motion (Le Gall, *Brownian Motion, Martingales, and Stochastic Calculus*, Chapter 1).
nodes.title: Fourth moment of a centered Gaussian

nodes.summary: A pre-Brownian motion `B` with measurable coordinates satisfies `E |B s - B t|⁴ ≤ 3 |s - t|²` for all times `s, t`, that is, it is a Kolmogorov process with exponents `p = 4`, `q = 2` and constant `3`: the moment hypothesis of Kolmogorov's lemma (Le Gall, DEA notes 1994, Lemme 2.3), with `d = 1` and `ε = 1`.
